The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service has rescued a 70-year-old woman who fell into a 60-foot-deep well at Oworonshoki, in the Kosofe Local Government Area of the state. The septuagenarian was rescued alive by firefighters from the Oworonshoki Fire Station following a distress call in the early hours of Sunday. The Controller-General of the service, Margaret Adeseye, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday. Adeseye stated that the incident occurred at 37 Abiola Street, Oworonshoki, adding that firefighters promptly responded to the distress call and successfully brought the woman out of the well. She stated, “The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service has rescued a 70-year-old woman who accidentally fell into a well about 60 feet deep at 37 Abiola Street, Oworonshoki, Kosofe LGA, Lagos. This is not the first time an open well accident has occurred in Lagos. PUNCH Metro reported on October 20 that a man died while attempting to rescue a two-year-old child who fell into a domestic well at Abule Egba, Lagos State. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, in a statement by its Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, said that the incident occurred at Paul Street, inward Agbe Road, Abule Egba. Oke-Osanyintolu noted that the toddler, whose mother worked as a cleaner in the compound, accidentally fell into the well, prompting a resident from the community to descend in an attempt to save the child.
